_comment: Scoped permissions for unattended loop.sh runs in THIS repo only.
It grants exactly what an iteration needs and nothing more, so you do NOT have to
reach for PERMISSION_MODE=bypassPermissions, which approves everything including
network calls and rm -rf.
PATCHED for the macOS port (2026-08-21):
Bare `dotnet` on this Mac resolves to /usr/local/share/dotnet, which CANNOT see
the .NET 10 SDK installed at ~/.dotnet. Every build command must use the absolute
path ~/.dotnet/dotnet. Both forms are allowed below so a stray bare call still
works, but the spec's verification array uses the absolute path deliberately.
Full rationale: MACOS-PORT-README.md.
GIT PUSH POLICY (2026-08-22): pushing feature branches and opening pull requests is
allowed without asking. Pushing to main/master, force-pushing, deleting remote
branches, merging or approving a PR, and changing repo settings are all denied.
Work reaches main only through a PR a human approves.
THE DENY LIST IS A SPEED BUMP, NOT A WALL. These rules match the literal command
STRING, not its meaning. `git push origin main` is blocked; a bare `git push`
while HEAD is already on main is NOT, because the rule cannot see the current
branch. `git push origin somebranch:main` also writes to main and matches nothing.
FORK TRAP, verified here 2026-08-22: this clone has both `origin` (the fork) and
`upstream` (NoahStolk). `gh repo view` resolves to UPSTREAM, so a bare
`gh pr create` opens a pull request against NoahStolk/ddinfo-tools - a public
action against someone else's project. ALWAYS pass
`--repo zeno-blade-creator/ddinfo-tools --base main` explicitly.
The real guard is server-side branch protection on the remote:
github.com/zeno-blade-creator/ddinfo-tools > Settings > Branches > Add rule >
Require a pull request before merging. That cannot be bypassed by any local
command. Until that is on, these rules are the only thing standing on main.
Review this list. Anything you are not comfortable with an agent running
unsupervised in this directory should be deleted from it.
